Cisco’s valuation has stretched across earnings, EBIT, EBITDA, revenue, and price-to-book metrics, pricing in significant operational execution and growth expectations [1]. Cisco’s near-term growth narrative is heavily contingent on AI infrastructure spending. Excluding AI contributions, Cisco’s guidance collapses to approximately 4% revenue growth, revealing underlying saturation in traditional networking and campus switching markets [1]. The company’s $28 billion acquisition of Splunk carries substantial integration risk; while strategically coherent for building unified telemetry and AI-driven observability, financial synergies are not expected to materialize until 2026–2027, and the deal has already compressed free cash flow (dropping to $1.54 billion in Q2 FY2026) [4], [9]. Activist positioning has amplified downside volatility.
